It started as a reasonable requirement. Build a 5-step wizard for calculating manufacturing costs. Each step captures a different cost category out of which 2 of the steps are complex as they involve a dynamic list of cost line items, where each line can be based on one of three material types: SAP materials (fetched live from SAP), custom materials (a different product category with its own validation rules) and dummy materials (master data stored in the application itself, used for estimation).
Each material type has different fields, different validators and different business rules. Switching a row from SAP to dummy clears some fields and carries over others. The user can add as many rows as they need — there’s no cap.
On paper it is pretty straight forward, a FormArray where each row is a FormGroup, with a type selector that drives which validators are active. Standard stuff.
In practice: one of the most instructive debugging experiences I have gone through so far.
